paraphrase: The courtesan Vasumitrā teaches a liberation 'free of passion': beings who come to her with passion leave free of passion — by seeing her, speaking with her, holding her hand or embracing her they attain various samādhis.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase. Narrative of skillful means; not a practice instruction.

paraphrase: Mañjuśrī tells Sudhana that to accomplish the bodhisattva's conduct he must seek, serve and honor spiritual friends without weariness, and sends him south to the monk Meghaśrī; the bodhisattva's knowledge comes from good friends.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase.

paraphrase: On Mount Potalaka Avalokiteśvara teaches Sudhana the bodhisattva liberation of the door of great compassion, by which he appears before beings to free them from fear.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase.

paraphrase: Māyā, the Buddha's mother, has the liberation of the illusory manifestation of great knowledge (or great vow): she has been and will be the mother of all the buddhas of the aeon.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase.

paraphrase: Maitreya opens the great tower called Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha; entering it Sudhana sees within it innumerable towers, each containing all the others and all of Maitreya's past lives and deeds, without obstruction; when Maitreya snaps his fingers the vision ends.
notes: Passage located and read in the local e-text (see location.section); paraphrase by U39 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: Mañjuśrī, stretching his hand across a hundred and ten yojanas, touches Sudhana's head: without faith the roots are weak and one does not know the dharma's depth; he then enables him to see Samantabhadra.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase.

paraphrase: Sudhana sees Samantabhadra and enters his body, where he travels through countless worlds and becomes equal to Samantabhadra and the buddhas; the verses of Samantabhadra's vows of good conduct (Bhadracarī) follow.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase.
